experiment_A.summary: 70% of DEV covered windows and 100% of the 201 lost windows possess exactly ONE good candidate. Pruning drops candidates that are ranked ranks 5-8 (78.6%) and heavily concentrated in slots 14 & 15 (45.8%), because farthest-point clustering leaps over viable moderate-probability modes to pick extreme geometric outliers.

experiment_B.summary: Duplicate8 yields exactly 0 rescues (proving candidate count alone cannot improve coverage). Jitter8 yields only 4-9 rescues. K22 rescues 25-30 windows (52-62.5% of K28) with 0 lost windows. K24 rescues 39-46 windows (81-95.8% of K28) with 0 lost windows. Progression from K20 to K22/K24 is highly superior to aggressive pruning.

experiment_C.summary: Across the 25-cell PCA/kNN grid and 1000 bootstrap iterations, R_support fluctuates in [1.188, 1.350] with 95% CI [1.210, 1.311]. R_support is never in the 1.05-1.15 regime. Forcing a purely conditional classification based on 1.248 vs 1.25 was an artifact of point evaluation. The robust conclusion is support + mapping mixed shift.

overall_recommendation.next_scientific_step: Adopt K22/K24 proposal conditioning instead of destructive K20 pruning; design Stage 04 conditioned head addressing both covariate support shift and conditional mapping mismatch simultaneously.
